newsitem.title: JAPAN: No big weakness in Japan economy - Sakakibara quoted.
newsitem.headline: No big weakness in Japan economy - Sakakibara quoted.

text.p: Eisuke Sakakibara, director-general of the Finance Ministry's International Finance Bureau, was quoted as saying on Wednesday that he sees no major weakness in the Japanese economy.
"I do not see any major weakness in the Japanese economy," Sakakibara told the International Herald Tribune in an interview.
"So I think this pessimism is groundless to a substantial degree and quite irrational. I am not saying that the recovery is very robust but that it is proceeding steadily," he said.

Despite imminent tax increases, the Japanese economy is in the midst of significant structural changes and is poised for steady recovery based on strong domestic growth, Sakakibara was quoted as saying.
He denied that Japan would attempt to rekindle growth through exports, the newspaper said.
Although economic growth is expected to slow after the tax increase next month, Sakakibara was quoted as saying that this would only be temporary.

Japanese consumers have known about the tax hike for months and have already factored it into their spending plans, he said, adding that consumer spending and economic growth would recover in the second half of the fiscal year starting from April 1, the paper said.
He expects the Japanese economy to grow by at least 1.9 percent in 1997/98, in line with government forecasts, the paper said.

Sakakibara was quoted as saying that the bulk of people still negative about Japan's prospects were the Japanese themselves. The paper said that many private Japanese economists expect growth of as little as one percent in 1997/98.
Sakakibara also noted that the United States has reservations about the strength of the Japanese economy, it said.
He said the Japanese economy would benefit most over the next few years from strong government support for major restructuring in the manufacturing, financial and public sectors, the paper said.
